userStories.title: Build the pure replay reconstruction core
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build the pure replay model and reconstruction core that turns persisted log/metrics/status inputs into a `RunTimeline` with inferred phases and degraded crashed-run handling.

**Motivation** — Debugging a failed run today means hand-reading raw JSONL.

**Approach** — The clean `story:step` event is bus-only and never persisted, so `inferPhases` derives the phase timeline from log signals that *are* in the JSONL, per this defined contract:

- **Phase pass:** `stage === "story-orchestrator"`, message `"Phase passed: <op>"` → a `PhaseStep { name: <op>, status: "pass" }`, in log order.
- **Phase fail:** `stage === "story-orchestrator"`, message `"Phase failed: <op>"` → a `PhaseStep { name: <op>, status: "fail" }`. This is the signal a failed story's root-cause phase is derived from.
- **Escalation occurrence:** `stage === "agent-manager"`, message containing `"fail-stale"` → an escalation marker on the story (authoritative tier values come from `StoryMetrics.finalTier`, not from inference).
- **Fix cycle:** `stage === "findings.cycle"` iteration records → a fix-cycle count (corroborated by `StoryMetrics.attempts` / `firstPassSuccess`).

`inferPhases` does **not** decide story pass/fail — `reconstruct` takes that from `StoryMetrics.success` or, when metrics are absent, from `status.json`. The report states that phases are reconstructed from logs (best-effort), not read from an exact event record.

**Scope** — In: `src/replay/types.ts` (`RunTimeline` / `StoryTimeline` / `PhaseStep`), `phase-infer.ts` (`inferPhases`), `reconstruct.ts` (`reconstructTimeline`), `index.ts` barrel, and graceful degrade for crashed runs. Out: any filesystem discovery, report rendering, JSON serialization, or CLI wiring.

**Interface**
```typescript
src/replay/types.ts (`RunTimeline` / `StoryTimeline` / `PhaseStep`)
src/replay/phase-infer.ts (`inferPhases`)
src/replay/reconstruct.ts (`reconstructTimeline`)
src/replay/index.ts
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `inferPhases` as a callable function.

[inferPhases] returns a phase list containing an entry with `name === "implementer"` and `status === "pass"` when given a log-entry array containing `{ stage: "story-orchestrator", message: "Phase passed: implementer", data: { storyId: "US-002" } }` and called as `inferPhases(entries, "US-002")`.
[inferPhases] returns phase names exactly `["test-writer", "implementer"]` in that order when given `Phase passed: test-writer` followed by `Phase passed: implementer` for `storyId "US-002"`.

[inferPhases] returns a phase list containing an entry with `name === "full-suite-gate"` and `status === "fail"` when given `{ stage: "story-orchestrator", message: "Phase failed: full-suite-gate", data: { storyId: "US-002" } }`.
[inferPhases] returns a non-empty escalation list for `US-002` when given an entry `{ stage: "agent-manager", message: "fail-stale: immediate same-agent retry", data: { storyId: "US-002" } }`.
Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `reconstructTimeline`.

[reconstructTimeline] returns a `RunTimeline` whose `runId` and `feature` equal the metrics and registry values and whose `stories` length equals the number of stories in the matching `RunMetrics` entry when given a parsed log spine plus a matching `RunMetrics` entry.

[reconstructTimeline] returns a `StoryTimeline` with `status === "passed"`, `finalTier === "balanced"`, `cost === 0.42`, and `attempts === 2` when the matching `StoryMetrics` entry has `success: true, finalTier: "balanced", cost: 0.42, attempts: 2`.

[reconstructTimeline] returns a `RunTimeline` with `status === "crashed"` and `StoryTimeline.cost === undefined` for each story when given a log spine and a `status.json` object carrying a crash signal but no matching `RunMetrics` entry.
[reconstructTimeline] returns `rootCausePhaseIndex` equal to the index of the inferred failed phase when a story has `success: false` and its inferred phases end in a phase with `status === "fail"`.
[reconstructTimeline] returns `inferred === true` on the `RunTimeline`.
[reconstructTimeline] returns `naxVersion === "0.71.1"` when the log spine includes `{ stage: "run.start", data: { naxVersion: "0.71.1" } }`.

routing.reasoning: This story creates the new replay model, phase inference, and reconstruction core across several modules and has to reconcile log-only and metrics-backed outcomes without I/O.

userStories.title: Add run discovery for replay
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a dedicated replay discovery layer that resolves a run query to registry metadata plus the backing JSONL path.

**Motivation** — `nax replay` turns that into a structured, failure-focused view so operators can diagnose the adversarial-review whack-a-mole problem (#1157), tune escalation, and see where a run went wrong — cheaply, from data that already exists on disk.

**Approach** — `src/replay/discovery.ts` (`discoverRun`): registry scan, prefix match, latest-default, not-found error. Mirrors `resolveRunFileFromRegistry` but returns `{ meta, jsonlPath }`; `getRunsDir()` via an injected dep.

**Scope** — In: registry scan, prefix-match semantics, latest-default behavior, returning `{ meta, jsonlPath }`, and `RUN_NOT_FOUND` error handling. Out: timeline reconstruction, report rendering, JSON output, or CLI registration.

**Interface**
```typescript
src/replay/discovery.ts (`discoverRun`): registry scan, prefix match, latest-default, not-found error. Mirrors `resolveRunFileFromRegistry` but returns `{ meta, jsonlPath }`; `getRunsDir()` via an injected dep.
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `discoverRun`.

[discoverRun] resolves to an object whose `meta.feature` equals the registry meta feature and whose `jsonlPath` ends in `.jsonl` when given an injected runs-dir containing a `<dir>/meta.json` whose `runId` equals the query and called as `discoverRun("run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z")`.
[discoverRun] resolves to that same run when called as `discoverRun("run-2026-07-04")` and the registry entry's `meta.runId` starts with the query.
[discoverRun] resolves to the registry entry whose `runId` is lexicographically greatest when called with no argument and given two registry entries.
[discoverRun] throws a `NaxError` with `code === "RUN_NOT_FOUND"` when no registry entry matches the query.
[discoverRun] throws a `NaxError` with `code === "RUN_NOT_FOUND"` when more than one registry entry matches the supplied run-id prefix.

routing.reasoning: This story adds one focused registry-scanning helper that mirrors existing `logs-reader` behavior but returns richer data and explicit replay errors.

userStories.title: Render the failure-focused replay report
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build the terminal renderer that turns a reconstructed `RunTimeline` into the failure-focused report described by the spec.

**Motivation** — Debugging a failed run today means hand-reading raw JSONL.

**Approach** — `src/replay/report.ts` (`renderReport`): default (passed collapsed / failed expanded), `--all`, `--story`, root-cause marker, best-effort notice, crashed-run header. Consumes `RunTimeline`.

**Scope** — In: default failed-expand/passed-collapse rendering, `--all`, `--story`, root-cause marker, header summary, best-effort notice, and crashed-run placeholders. Out: file discovery, reconstruction, JSON serialization, or CLI option parsing.

**Interface**
```typescript
src/replay/report.ts (`renderReport`): default (passed collapsed / failed expanded), `--all`, `--story`, root-cause marker, best-effort notice, crashed-run header. Consumes `RunTimeline`.
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `renderReport`.

[renderReport] returns a string containing the passed story's id on a single summary line and the failed story's inferred phase names on their own lines when given a `RunTimeline` with one `passed` and one `failed` story and default options.
Given default options, [renderReport] returns no per-phase lines for a `passed` story and includes the failed story's phases.
[renderReport] returns a string containing a passed story's phase names when called with `{ all: true }`.
[renderReport] returns a string containing US-002's block and not containing any other story id when called with `{ story: "US-002" }`.
[renderReport] returns a string containing the text `root cause` on the failed terminal phase line when a failed story's terminal phase has `status: "fail"`.
[renderReport] returns a header containing the `runId`, the `feature`, the run `status`, the story count, and the total cost.
[renderReport] returns a string containing the best-effort notice indicating phases were reconstructed from logs.

[renderReport] returns a string whose header contains `CRASHED` and that renders a placeholder for missing cost without throwing when given a `RunTimeline` with `status: "crashed"` and a story whose `cost` is `undefined`.

routing.reasoning: This story is a single presentation module over the replay model with option-driven output branches but no new persistence or command wiring.

userStories.title: Wire JSON output and the replay CLI command
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the serializer and thin CLI orchestration that discovers a run, reconstructs the timeline, renders the report or JSON, and registers `nax replay` in the main commander entrypoint.

**Motivation** — `nax replay` turns that into a structured, failure-focused view so operators can diagnose the adversarial-review whack-a-mole problem (#1157), tune escalation, and see where a run went wrong — cheaply, from data that already exists on disk.

**Approach** — `src/replay/json.ts` (`toReplayJson`), `src/commands/replay.ts` (`runReplay` orchestrator + `registerReplayCommand`), wired into `bin/nax.ts`. Exit codes; crashed-run end-to-end.

**Scope** — In: JSON serialization, orchestrator dependencies, stdout/stderr writers, exit codes, command registration, `--json`, `--story`, `--all`, and crashed-run end-to-end behavior. Out: changes to live run persistence or any new artifact formats.

**Interface**
```typescript
src/replay/json.ts (`toReplayJson`)
src/commands/replay.ts (`runReplay` orchestrator + `registerReplayCommand`)
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `toReplayJson`.
[toReplayJson] returns an object whose `runId`, `feature`, and `status` equal the timeline's and whose `stories` array length equals `timeline.stories.length` when given a `RunTimeline`.
Given a stubbed `discoverRun`, when `runReplay("run-x", {})` is called, then `discoverRun` is invoked once with `"run-x"`.

Given stubbed `discoverRun` and file reads that yield a known `RunTimeline`, when `runReplay(query, {})` is called, then `renderReport` is invoked once with a timeline whose `runId` matches the known value.
Given the same stubs, when `runReplay(query, { json: true })` is called, then `toReplayJson` is invoked, its serialization is written to the injected output writer, and `renderReport` is not invoked.
Given `@/replay` or the command module is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `registerReplayCommand`.
[registerReplayCommand] adds a subcommand named `replay` that accepts an optional positional run-id and exposes a `--json` option when applied to a fresh commander `Command` instance.

Given `discoverRun` throws `NaxError { code: "RUN_NOT_FOUND" }`, when `runReplay("missing", {})` is called, then it resolves to exit code `1` and writes a message containing `"missing"` to the injected error writer.

Given a JSONL file containing malformed lines alongside valid entries, when `runReplay(query, {})` is called, then it skips the malformed lines, writes a report from the remaining spine, and resolves to exit code `0`.

Given an injected registry and files for a run with a crash signal and no metrics entry, when `runReplay(query, {})` is called, then it writes a report whose header contains `CRASHED` to the injected output writer and resolves to exit code `0`.

routing.reasoning: This wiring story mainly composes already-built replay helpers into one command, serializer, and commander registration path using existing CLI patterns.

analysis:
This is an additive CLI feature in an existing Bun + TypeScript codebase, not a greenfield app. There is no existing `src/replay/` module today, so the feature should land as a new bounded subsystem plus thin CLI wiring rather than being folded into `logs` or `runs`; `rtk rg --files src | rtk rg '^src/replay/'` returns no matches. The current run-registry SSOT already exists in `getRunsDir()` and must be reused instead of rejoining `~/.nax` manually; it resolves `process.env.NAX_RUNS_DIR ?? join(globalConfigDir(), "runs")` in `src/utils/paths.ts:27-29`. Registry metadata is already persisted by `wireRegistry()` as `MetaJson { runId, project, feature, workdir, statusPath, eventsDir, registeredAt }` in `src/pipeline/subscribers/registry.ts:19-25` and `src/pipeline/subscribers/registry.ts:45-67`, which gives replay the authoritative path to `status.json` and the feature-local `runs/` JSONL directory.

The existing closest command is `logs`. `resolveRunFileFromRegistry()` in `src/commands/logs-reader.ts:22-55` already scans `<getRunsDir()>/<entry>/meta.json`, prefix-matches with `meta.runId === runId || meta.runId.startsWith(runId)`, skips unreadable `meta.json`, and then resolves the `.jsonl` file from `eventsDir`. It throws a generic `Error` on miss and returns only a `string | null`, which is insufficient for replay because replay also needs `MetaJson`, latest-default selection, and explicit not-found semantics. That is the main rationale for a parallel `discoverRun()` instead of extending `resolveRunFileFromRegistry()` directly. The `runs` command at `src/commands/runs.ts:113-222` is useful precedent for registry iteration, sorting, and graceful handling of unreadable `statusPath`; it also shows repo style for `_deps` injection via `_runsCmdDeps` at `src/commands/runs.ts:23-27`.

The persisted timeline spine already exists in `LogEntry` and human-log formatting. `LogEntry` in `src/logger/types.ts:9-27` carries `timestamp`, `level`, `stage`, `message`, optional `storyId`, optional `sessionRole`, and optional structured `data`; replay reconstruction should treat this JSONL as the ordered source of truth. Human formatting should reuse the exported `formatLogEntry()` SSOT in `src/log-format/formatter.ts:91-132` instead of inventing a second entry renderer. The formatter file also exports reusable `formatDuration()` and `formatCost()` helpers at `src/log-format/formatter.ts:46-63`, but the spec explicitly calls out that `runs.ts` table helpers are private, so replay should either call the public formatter helpers or keep local presentation helpers rather than importing private functions from `runs.ts`.

The exact phase signals replay needs already exist in the codebase. `formatPhaseResultMessage()` returns the persisted strings `Phase passed: <op>` / `Phase failed: <op>` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator-logging.ts:15`, and those strings are covered by unit tests in `test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator-logging.test.ts:6-10` and `test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator.test.ts:1629-1637`. Fail-stale escalation markers are logged from the agent manager with messages including `"fail-stale: immediate same-agent retry"` and `"fail-stale: no swap candidate, returning terminal failure"` at `src/agents/manager.ts:309-315` and `src/agents/manager.ts:352-356`, so replay can infer escalation occurrences from persisted logs without reaching into live execution code. Fix-cycle iterations are already emitted as `stage === "findings.cycle"` with `message === "iteration completed"` in `src/findings/cycle.ts:477`, and the curator collector already parses those exact signals from run JSONL in `src/plugins/builtin/curator/collect.ts:428-454`. That collector is strong evidence that replay should read log lines leniently and infer from message/stage pairs rather than expecting a richer event bus record.

Metrics enrichment is already available but optional. `StoryMetrics` in `src/metrics/types.ts:98-200` provides authoritative `attempts`, `finalTier`, `success`, `cost`, `durationMs`, `firstPassSuccess`, and reviewer severity buckets under `reviewMetrics.*.findingsBySeverity`; `RunMetrics` at `src/metrics/types.ts:235-263` adds run-level `totalCost`, `totalStories`, `storiesFailed`, and `totalDurationMs`. `loadRunMetrics(outputDir)` loads `outputDir/metrics.json` and returns an array in `src/metrics/tracker.ts:344-349`, so replay needs to filter by `runId` rather than assume one metrics file per run. The spec’s crashed-run behavior matches existing reality: metrics can be absent because writes happen during completion, and `status.json` remains the crash-status fallback. `NaxStatusFile` already includes `run.status` with `"completed" | "failed" | "stalled" | "crashed" | ...` and crash metadata `crashedAt` / `crashSignal` in `src/execution/status-file.ts:57-80`, plus current progress counts in `src/execution/status-file.ts:82-96`. Replay should therefore prefer `RunMetrics` for success/failure counts when present and degrade to `status.json` when absent.

Review-audit data is also already on disk and keyed by run/story. `persistReviewAudit()` writes JSON files under `<outputDir>/review-audit/<featureName>/` or `<projectRoot>/.nax/review-audit/<featureName>/` in `src/review/review-audit.ts:168-181`. Persisted entries include `runId`, `storyId`, `reviewer`, `passed`, and advisory/blocking findings payloads via `toPersistedEntry()` in `src/review/review-audit.ts:139-165`. That makes replay’s review enrichment feasible without any live-run changes, but it also creates a discovery risk: there is no single helper today that loads review-audit files for a run, so the new replay discovery/orchestration layer will need to scan the feature audit directory and filter by `runId` itself.

Existing CLI wiring is centralized in `bin/nax.ts`. `logs` is registered as a direct `program.command("logs")` block at `bin/nax.ts:1299-1333`, and `runs` is registered similarly at `bin/nax.ts:1399-1451`. Replay should follow that pattern and be registered alongside those commands, not via a separate CLI entrypoint. The command barrel `src/commands/index.ts:17-20` currently exports `logsCommand`, `precheckCommand`, `runsCommand`, and `unlockCommand`; if repo conventions expect barrel export parity for commands, replay should likely add `runReplay` and/or `registerReplayCommand` there as well. The existing `logs` integration test pattern in `test/integration/cli/cli-core-logs.test.ts:87-233` is especially relevant because it tests the command function directly, injects a temporary registry via `NAX_RUNS_DIR`, and captures console output without subprocess startup. Replay integration tests should mirror that shape for unknown runs, prefix matching, `--json`, and crashed-run output.

Primary files that will need modification are `bin/nax.ts` for commander registration, and likely `src/commands/index.ts` if the new command should be re-exported. New files will carry most of the work: `src/replay/types.ts`, `src/replay/phase-infer.ts`, `src/replay/reconstruct.ts`, `src/replay/discovery.ts`, `src/replay/report.ts`, `src/replay/json.ts`, `src/replay/index.ts`, and `src/commands/replay.ts`. Because the spec makes the reconstruction core pure and I/O-free, the target architecture is a four-layer split: pure model/types + inference, artifact discovery/loading, rendering/serialization, then a thin command orchestrator. That split matches existing repo conventions around thin command files and pure helper modules.

The biggest implementation risks are behavioral rather than mechanical. First, discovery must not hardcode `~/.nax` or duplicate path logic; it must depend on `getRunsDir()` (`src/utils/paths.ts:27-29`) and mirror registry semantics. Second, phase inference is explicitly best-effort because the event-bus `story:step` record is not persisted; replay should never overclaim precision or treat inferred phases as authoritative story outcomes. Third, malformed or truncated JSONL needs to be skipped line-by-line, matching existing lenient readers in `src/commands/logs-reader.ts:90-139`. Fourth, replay needs consistent error typing: there is a base `NaxError` with `{ message, code, context }` in `src/errors.ts:11-20`, but no existing `RUN_NOT_FOUND` subclass, so the new command will likely either instantiate `new NaxError(..., "RUN_NOT_FOUND", ...)` or add a dedicated error class. Fifth, adding a new top-level command must not regress current `logs`/`runs` behavior or import cycles; the formatter file already documents a circular-import hazard around barrels in `src/log-format/formatter.ts:11-17`, so replay should keep imports leaf-oriented.

Current test coverage around adjacent seams is solid. `test/integration/cli/cli-core-logs.test.ts:118-233` covers registry-driven command behavior and temporary run fixtures; `test/unit/log-format/formatter.test.ts:88-100` already exercises story-orchestrator phase lines; `test/unit/plugins/builtin/curator-collector.test.ts:259-370` demonstrates how real metrics, review-audit, and JSONL artifacts are synthesized together in tests. Those are the best templates for replay fixtures. There is no migration path for existing users beyond adding a new `nax replay` command; the feature is read-only and backward-compatible because it consumes artifacts already being written today. The only operator-facing behavior change is improved post-mortem visibility for existing runs, including crashed runs whose metrics are incomplete.
